entries.text: If a "put" action repeatedly fails despite being at the correct location and holding the object, try the alternative phrasing "move <object> to <receptacle>"; if that also fails, try a different valid receptacle of the same type, and if the receptacle is a container, ensure it is open first.
When the task asks for two objects, place the first before taking the second, so that a full hand cannot block the second take.
To clean something, carry it to the sinkbasin, hold it, and say clean <object> with the sinkbasin in reach; a refusal means the object is not in hand or you are not at the basin.
To heat something, put it in the microwave and close it before saying heat <object>; the microwave has to be opened again before you can take the object out.
To cool something, put it in the fridge and say cool <object>; the fridge may stay open, and the object has to be in hand when the cooling happens.
To examine something under a lamp, take the object first, go to the desklamp, turn it on, and only then say examine <object>; turning the lamp on is not the task.
